about: New Holland Borough sits along Route 23 in Earl Township, right in the middle of eastern Lancaster County. It has always been a working community. The New Holland name itself is tied to decades of agricultural equipment manufacturing, and the industrial and commercial mix in and around the borough reflects that history. There are manufacturing plants, feed suppliers, construction companies, churches, and the kind of Route 23 retail strip that keeps the town busy throughout the week.

Asphalt in New Holland takes a beating. Industrial facilities with constant forklift and semi traffic wear down lot surfaces much faster than typical commercial or residential use. Couple that with eastern Lancaster County winters and you get surfaces that need attention more frequently than a lot of property managers plan for. We see it every spring when we come out here. Lots that looked passable in October have new potholes and significant cracking by April.

about: Denver Borough sits on Route 272 at the northern edge of Lancaster County, just south of the Berks County line near Adamstown. Driveways that looked fine in October have new cracks running through them by April, and parking lots that were already overdue for sealing are showing real structural wear.
